american-express-gold-card: Loved for 4x earning on dining and groceries; many find the annual fee the main sticking point.
blue-cash-preferred-card: Praised for high cash back on groceries and streaming; few real complaints.
capital-one-savor: Loved for high cash back on dining, entertainment and groceries; a few report accounts closed.
capital-one-venture-x: Valued for a travel credit and miles that offset the fee; some find the portal-only credit cumbersome.
chase-freedom-flex: Liked for rotating bonus categories and stackable offers; some find the categories a hassle to track.
chase-freedom-unlimited: Liked as an everyday catch-all with bonus dining rewards; some say it feels less competitive now.
citi-double-cash: Liked as a simple flat-rate catch-all kept for years; many find Citi customer service the main complaint.
everydollar: Liked as a simple zero-based monthly budget; some find it clunky and want bank sync, which is not free.
fidelity-brokerage-account: Praised for great service and everything in one place; a sizable minority report held transfers.
fidelity-cash-management-account: Valued as a dependable main checking account with free ATMs; many find bill pay and transfers slow.
freetaxusa: Praised as easy, cheap and accurate with free federal filing; a few missed direct imports.
monarch: Liked for its interface and Mint-style overview; many find accounts that stop syncing the top complaint.
the-platinum-card-from-american-express: Valued for lounges, hotel stays and credits; others call it a coupon book that is hard to use.
wells-fargo-active-cash: Liked as a simple flat-rate catch-all with a solid bonus; some find redemption rules limiting.
wise: Liked for low, upfront fees and good exchange rates; many find held transfers frustrating.
